subtitle: A craving rises, crests and falls. Here are tools to ride it out.
fourDsBody: Four moves that break the craving loop. Pick one and use it now.
dsDelayBody: Promise yourself you will do nothing for 10-20 minutes. Most cravings peak and fall on their own.
dsDistractBody: Change activity: go for a walk, play something that occupies hands and mind, call someone.
dsDeepBody: Exhale longer than you inhale. Six slow breaths activate your body's calming system.
dsDecatBody: Tell yourself: "It's a craving, not an order." You can feel it without obeying it. This feeling is temporary.
distColdWater: Splash cold water on your face or put ice on your wrists
distCall: Text or call a trusted person (talk about their life, not only yours)
distShower: Take a shower: hot or cold, whatever shifts your state
distMusic: Put on a loud song and move
distClean: Tidy something small: a drawer, the desk
distGame: Play a visuospatial game (puzzle, Tetris, something absorbing)
distJournal: Write 5 lines about what you feel in your body
distPet: Play with or pet an animal
distStretch: Stretch for 2 minutes: neck, shoulders, back
coldBody: Cold on the face triggers the dive reflex and calms the nervous system: cold water on the face for 15-30 seconds, or ice on cheeks and forehead (with a cloth). Do not use with certain heart conditions without asking a doctor.
logBody: Tracking the urges you ride out builds self-efficacy: it is your best metric.
surfSubtitle: A craving does not last forever. If you don't feed it, it peaks and falls.
phaseObserve: Observe: without judgment, like watching a wave come in.
phaseLocate: Locate it in your body: where do you feel it? Tight, burning, tingling?
phaseBreathe: Breathe: soft inhale, longer exhale. The wave is still rising, and you are still here.
phaseFall: Watch the wave fall. You don't have to do anything else.
surfHint: You can close your eyes. The wave rises, crests and falls: always.
surfDone: You did it. How is the craving now?
breathSubtitle: Inhale 4, hold 4, exhale 4, hold 4. Five minutes is enough to lower arousal.
triggersSubtitle: People, places, times and emotions that light up craving. For each one, have a plan.
triggerNamePlaceholder: E.g. the corner bar, Fridays, arguing with my boss
triggerPlanHint: What will you do when it shows up? Be concrete: "I walk out for 10 minutes and call Ana".
triggerEmpty: No triggers saved yet. Add your three most frequent ones.
